## Part 2 · 10:23

[10:23] The unexamined life is not worth living for a human being. It's not just poetic. It's a declaration of moral responsibility. Socrates is telling the court and us that a life lived on autopilot based merely on assumptions, inherited rituals, or untested ideologies is not truly a human life. To live without examining our values, our beliefs, our doubts, even our disbeliefs is to fall short of what reason demands from us. It's not just a personal choice. It's a philosophical duty. The charges against Socrates were three-fold.

[11:04] Not recognizing the gods of the city, introducing new divinities, and corrupting the youth. What he was doing was teaching Athenians to think, to challenge norms and traditions, to question sacred myths, and to examine inherited beliefs.
